exec: Political pressure is building over the outages; senior officials say they see no cyberattack.
plain: US politicians want answers about the run of outages. The homeland security chief and the spy chief say they see no sign of a cyberattack.

sources.name: BNN Bloomberg / CTV News live updates

summary: Lawmakers including Jeffries and Hawley are pressing for answers after outages at Microsoft, the FAA, banks, Apple and the NSA. DHS Secretary Mullin said he was 98 percent certain there was no cyberattack; DNI Clayton said it was not a coordinated nation-state effort. On 18 November officials told a House committee they had no evidence of malicious attacks; CyberScoop reports lawmakers linking the outages to rushed patching of AI-found flaws.
title: Washington reacts to the outages: lawmakers demand answers, DHS chief points to AI

validation.note: Political response reported by The National Desk, Newsweek, Nextgov and CyberScoop; hearing of 18 Nov read at Nextgov and CyberScoop.

review.note: Summary overstated: Trump did not explicitly deny an attack; Mullin said 98 percent certain no cyberattack, Clayton said not a coordinated nation-state effort; 18 Nov hearing says no evidence of malicious attacks; AI-patching link attributed to CyberScoop only. Reworded summary, plain, exec.
